aspects.says: acquire() goes before the try and release() in its finally, so a failed call gives its permit back and an interrupted acquire doesn't release a permit it never took.
basis: section:A Fixed Pool Was Also a Limit: Put a Semaphore in Front of What Is Scarce

aspects.says: A virtual thread is always a daemon at NORM_PRIORITY in the VirtualThreads group: setDaemon(false) throws, setPriority is ignored, and a virtual thread never keeps the JVM alive.
basis: section:A Virtual Thread Is Always a Daemon, at Normal Priority

aspects.says: On Java 21, -Djdk.tracePinnedThreads prints the stack where a pinned virtual thread blocked, and JFR records jdk.VirtualThreadPinned events.
basis: section:On Java 21, Blocking Inside synchronized Holds the Carrier

aspects.says: From JDK 24 (JEP 491) a virtual thread unmounts inside synchronized and while waiting to enter a monitor.
basis: section:On Java 21, Blocking Inside synchronized Holds the Carrier
aspects.reason: a version difference: practices run on Java 25, and no test may depend on behaviour that differs between 21 and 25

aspects.says: Thread.getAllStackTraces() and ThreadMXBean see only platform threads, so a gauge built on them reads 0 for virtual threads; count the work in the code that starts and ends it.
basis: section:Thread Listings Leave Virtual Threads Out

aspects.says: The permit is taken around each call to the resource, not around each task, and pooling virtual threads would limit tasks that never touch the resource.
basis: section:A Fixed Pool Was Also a Limit: Put a Semaphore in Front of What Is Scarce

aspects.says: On Java 21 a virtual thread that blocks inside synchronized, or waits to enter it, pins its carrier, the scheduler adds no carrier for it, and enough pinned threads stop every virtual thread in the JVM.
basis: section:On Java 21, Blocking Inside synchronized Holds the Carrier

aspects.says: A fixed pool also capped how many tasks reached a scarce resource at once; with one virtual thread per task that cap is gone, and a Semaphore sized to the resource puts it back.
basis: section:A Fixed Pool Was Also a Limit: Put a Semaphore in Front of What Is Scarce

aspects.says: A virtual thread that blocks in sleep, a java.util.concurrent lock or queue, or a socket read unmounts and frees its carrier, while a blocked platform thread holds its OS thread.
basis: section:A Blocked Virtual Thread Gives Its Carrier Back; a Blocked Platform Thread Keeps Its OS Thread
aspects.reason: which carrier runs a virtual thread, and when, is up to the scheduler, and the page states this difference without a run of its own (unit 6.7.1 owns the mechanism); the pinning question in the quiz builds on it
